name: The Slayer Crowned — Bhaal's Chosen Rises
era: 1492 DR — the winter the murder-god won his throne back. The Netherbrain fell, but in the same hour a defender who carried the Dark Urge embraced their birthright as the true Chosen of Bhaal, slew their way clear of the war, and gave the Lord of Murder a living hand in the world again. Ketheric Thorm and Enver Gortash are dead; Orin the Red is dead, supplanted. Keep the timeline straight: the Absolute is broken, but a new Bhaalspawn walks crowned in blood, and the Gate's nights have a patron once more. Do not raise the long-dead or pre-empt events that haven't happened.
premise_suffix: In this telling the brain was destroyed — and a darker thing took root in the ruins. A defender who had carried the Dark Urge all along surrendered to it, claimed the mantle of Bhaal's true Chosen, and ended the war with a coronation of murder. Now the Lord of Murder has a living instrument in Baldur's Gate again: the Bhaalist cult walks bolder, ritual killings mark the calendar, and the city's relief is shot through with quiet terror. Into a Gate where the dark has a name and a patron, the player steps: a nobody whose anonymity is the only thing between them and a god's appetite — and perhaps the only blade close enough to matter.
standing_threads: The crowned Bhaalspawn: a living Chosen of Bhaal rules the Gate's nights from the shadows, and ritual murder has become a slow, deliberate liturgy written across the city.
The bolder cult: Bhaalist murder-shrines no longer hide; the Lord of Murder's faithful gather openly in the Outer City, and the Flaming Fist is too frightened or too infiltrated to stop them.
The hunt for the Slayer: Harpers, Gur, and grief-mad survivors search for the Chosen's true name and mortal weakness — while the cult hunts the hunters in turn.
history_append: The Urge embraced: a defender who had fought the Dark Urge through the whole war gave in at its climax, claiming the murderous birthright of a true Bhaalspawn and butchering a path out of the chaos.
Orin supplanted: Orin the Red, Bhaal's prior Chosen, fell — and the new Bhaalspawn took her place at the head of the Lord of Murder's faith, more deliberate and far more dangerous.
The liturgy of murder: where the war left wounds, the new Chosen leaves art — ritual killings staged to honor Bhaal, each one tightening the cult's grip and the city's dread.
story_seeds_append: A string of ritual murders follows a pattern only the party notices; tracing it leads toward a name no one will say aloud — and toward the question of whether the Slayer can be killed by mortal hands at all.

A Bhaalist defector wants out and offers the location of the next sanctioned killing in exchange for protection — but betraying the Lord of Murder marks the defector, and anyone shielding them, for the knife.
The Gur hunters and a grieving Harper want the same thing for different reasons: the Chosen's death. Their methods are about to collide, and the cult means to bury them both.

npc-jaheira.where: the Harper safehouses, marshaling the resistance to the cult
npc-jaheira.note: Has buried too many to the Dead Three to abide a new Bhaalspawn crowned; the hardest, steadiest blade aimed at the murder-god's hand.

npc-minsc.where: the Gate, hunting evil he can finally see
npc-minsc.note: Knows Bhaal's work of old; throws himself at the cult with everything he has, and Boo, he swears, can smell a Bhaalspawn at fifty paces.

npc-astarion.where: the Outer City, where the cult grows boldest
npc-astarion.note: Survived two centuries of one monster's appetite and has no wish to feed another's; trades the resistance the cult's movements for a price.

npc-shadowheart.where: a shrine that stands against the murder-liturgy
npc-shadowheart.note: A goddess of loss is one thing; a god of murder crowned is another — her presence in a scene means a cleric's defiance of Bhaal is near.

npc-wyll.status: alive, the Blade against the knife
npc-wyll.where: the Gate, defending the city his father served
npc-wyll.note: A hero's oath against a murder-god's reign; throws his whole legend at the cult, his pact's price still a shadow on the work.

npc-karlach.where: between the cult and its next victim
npc-karlach.note: Stands in the door of the murder-god's appetite with an infernal engine for a heart; the cult fears her and she means to keep it that way.

npc-the-emperor.where: the underbelly, weighing the new Chosen
npc-the-emperor.note: A god's living hand is a variable to be priced; the mind flayer offers the hunt terrible help and serves, as ever, only itself.

npc-withers.where: where the murder-liturgy leaves its dead
npc-withers.note: Keeps the ledger of Bhaal's harvest; in his dust-dry way he seems to take the new Chosen as a personal affront, and aids those who would end it.

Gale.status: alive, lending his lore to the hunt
Gale.where: Sorcerous Sundries, researching how a Bhaalspawn dies
Gale.note: Pores over what the canon says of slaying a god's Chosen; the obvious mind to find the weakness, and a target the cult would dearly love to silence.

Lae'zel.where: striking at the cult wherever it surfaces
Lae'zel.note: Holds murder-worship in githyanki contempt; a ruthless, uncompromising edge aimed at the Slayer's faithful.

Halsin.where: the wilds and the Outer City margins
Halsin.note: Shelters those the cult would harvest and reads the land for where the murder-liturgy has fouled it; a healer's front against the dark.

arc_gates.note: Name the Slayer — Minsc means to sniff out the crowned Bhaalspawn's mortal name so the cult's god-touched head can be reached; win his trust and Boo points the way to the liturgy's author.
